identity.title: Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log and C-1 Outlet Detector-Tube Check — August and September 2026

scan.summary: This is a compliance record log documenting daily scrubber pressure-drop readings and weekly carbon-unit outlet detector-tube checks for August and September 2026, required by Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01. The log tracks two scrubbers (S-1 for acid repackaging, S-2 for caustic repackaging) and verifies they maintain pressures between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column and show no carbon breakthrough.
scan.freshness_note: This record covers August and September 2026, with the last entry on September 25, 2026. It is current as of today (September 29, 2026). The supervisor review and date signature lines remain blank and should be completed.

gaps.title: Missing supervisor sign-off
gaps.description: Both August and September logs show blank lines for supervisor review signature and date, which are required for record completion and permit compliance.
gaps.fix: Complete the supervisor review signature and date fields on both pages immediately.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Conditions 3.1 and 3.3
gaps.locator: Page 1 (August) signature line and Page 2 (September) signature line

gaps.title: Incomplete weekly detector-tube checks in September
gaps.description: The September detector-tube log shows only two entries (Sep 7 and Sep 21) when the condition requires weekly checks. September has five weeks and should have five weekly readings recorded.
gaps.fix: Add the missing detector-tube readings for the weeks of September 14 and September 28 (or the applicable weeks if a different schedule is used).
gaps.locator: Page 2, September weekly detector-tube check table
gaps.quote: Condition 3.3: weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet

gaps.title: One out-of-range scrubber reading — S-2 on September 9
gaps.description: On September 9, the S-2 (caustic line) scrubber pressure drop was recorded as 6.4 inches of water column, which exceeds the maximum permitted range of 6.0 inches.
gaps.fix: Document the cause of the pressure exceedance (e.g., nozzle clogging, line blockage, instrumentation error) and any corrective action taken. This may require notification to Oregon DEQ depending on permit language for exceedances.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1: keep pressure drop between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column whenever the line is operating
gaps.quote: keep it between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column whenever the line is operating

scan.confidence_notes: I read the document directly and identified one clear permit violation (Sep 9 pressure reading of 6.4 in. w.c., exceeding the 6.0 maximum). The record shows a significant gap between reported operating days and logged entries in August (21 and 20 days operating vs. 16 entries), which raises questions about whether daily readings were actually taken and recorded as required. September readings are more complete but still need final supervisor sign-off. I am not certain whether the weekly detector-tube schedule in September is intentionally bi-weekly (two entries per month) or whether it should have five entries; this depends on the actual permit language which I do not have. The supervisor sign-off fields are blank and must be completed. The document itself is readable and in good condition.
